## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: young drivers, permits, license classes, renewals, ID cards and fees
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical handbook page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The driver's education page twice points readers to Chapter 4 for night driving, but the contents list places Night Driving in Chapter 5 (Special Driving Conditions); the cross-reference was not repeated and the night-hour minimums were taken only from the page itself [A02].
Motorcycle permit and license rules are on these pages but outside the Basic Class C scope; they appear only as scope-noted continuation blocks in part C2 [A06].
The human-trafficking page is public-safety outreach, not licensing law; only its red flags and the do-not-confront advice were kept, and its hotline numbers were left out as dynamic [A10].
Fees are printed with a statement that they are subject to change, so every fee is isolated as dynamic and must be re-checked before learners see it [A11].
Commercial license fees and endorsement details are scope-noted; only the general reinstatement rule was kept in part C.

corpus_stability.reason: The Nevada Driver's Handbook carries one edition line on its cover (DMV 700 March 2024) and one copyright year on its title page, with a short key-changes list; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year. The edition is about two and a half years old at intake, so currency is held as freshness debt in part A.
